summary: This clipped Snowflake documentation page describes the EVENT_USAGE_HISTORY view, which shows the history of data loaded into Snowflake event tables over the last 365 days for an entire account. It lists four columns: START_TIME, END_TIME, CREDITS_USED, and BYTES_INGESTED, each with its data type and meaning. The usage note says the view may lag by up to 180 minutes. Navigation and boilerplate text from the web page were ignored.
one_line: Reference for Snowflake's EVENT_USAGE_HISTORY view, which tracks event table data loads, credits billed, and bytes ingested over the past year.
key_facts: The EVENT_USAGE_HISTORY view can be used to query the history of data loaded into Snowflake event tables within the last 365 days (1 year).
The view displays the history of data loaded and credits billed for the entire Snowflake account.
START_TIME is a TIMESTAMP_LTZ column giving the start of the time range (in the UTC time zone) in which data loading took place.
END_TIME is a TIMESTAMP_LTZ column giving the end of the time range (in the UTC time zone) in which data loading took place.
CREDITS_USED is a NUMBER column giving the number of credits billed for loading data into the event table during the START_TIME and END_TIME window.
BYTES_INGESTED is a NUMBER column giving the number of bytes of data loaded during the START_TIME and END_TIME window.
Latency for the EVENT_USAGE_HISTORY view may be up to 180 minutes (3 hours).
The page refers readers to 'Setting up an Event Table' for more information about event tables.
The page refers readers to 'Logging and Tracing' for more information about logging and tracing.
